In /Users/cooper/Projects/taxkit/.claude/worktrees/taxkit-native-effect-alchemy-f44f82 (read-only, very thorough), map the API side. Report with file:line references and short excerpts:
1. apps/api: Cloudflare Worker entry (worker.application.ts etc.), how the app is built (HttpApiBuilder, HttpRouter, Alchemy Worker bridge, ALCHEMY_PHASE plan check), the private RPC/`calculatorRequest` capability (what path it admits — POST /rpc only?), bounded buffers (2 MiB, 10s deadline, 5s body read 64KiB, 5s work), catchCause sites (worker.application.ts private RPC buffer returning 503, mcp-response.boundary.ts), ErrorReporter usage, CORS config (allowed origins, headers, whether tracing is disabled to avoid preflight), MCP (modern/legacy, allowedOrigins, early origin/setup-quota protection), rate limit, Cache-Control headers set (list values), discovery documents (llms.txt etc., formatter), how API reads Website origin/Output.
2. Bun host: where it lives, how it composes the bounded calculation service (is a capacity pool created per request?), what protocols it serves.
3. packages/api/http: HttpApi declaration (TaxKitApi groups/endpoints with paths/methods — list all), exported helpers createTaxKitApiClient, withTaxKitHttpApiClient, createTaxKitApiClientLayer and aliases, who uses them (grep across repo incl. examples/docs-examples/sdk).
4. packages/api/rpc: RPC group, rate-identity.boundary.ts (Cloudflare header interpretation), bounded RPC client adapter that filters error statuses/reconstructs 200.
5. packages/calculators: TakeHomeScenarioLiveFromInput and AnnualTaxScenarioLiveFromInput signatures and callers; PublicCalculatorService location and methods.
6. packages/sdk/typescript: private Promise runtime, exports, packed-artifact / downstream validation commands.
7. packages/content: schemas.ts and live.layer.ts — origin settings (websiteOrigin/publicOrigin).
Keep it factual and compact (under ~2000 words).

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). ## plugin:paper-desktop:paper
Paper is a professional design tool for creating user interfaces. The user is working on a 2D canvas composing designs.
The Paper MCP server gives you tools to be a talented designer for web and mobile apps and websites. You can read designs from the user's file, see what the user is doing, and write HTML back into the design as new nodes.

You MUST load the full guide before other Paper tools: get_guide({ topic: "paper-mcp-instructions" }). Do this once per session; call again if a long thread may have dropped guide text.

- Call get_basic_info when starting on a file to learn artboards and dimensions; use get_selection to see user focus. Omit fileId to use the file the user is looking at, or call list_resources to find another.
- pageId defaults to the page the user is viewing; pass it to work on another page without disrupting them. You can't switch their page.
- Typography: you MUST call get_font_family_info before your first typographic styling in a session. Prefer font families listed in get_basic_info unless the user specifies otherwise. Use px for font sizes, em for letter-spacing, px for line-height.
- New designs: before writing HTML, generate a brief (palette, type scale, spacing, direction) unless given a design system.
- Creating/editing: each write_html call should add roughly one visual group; prefer duplicate_nodes with update_styles and set_text_content when faster than rewriting HTML.
- Quality: use get_screenshot to review after meaningful changes. Artboard height is a starting point — when content clips set height: "fit-content" via update_styles rather than guessing a fixed height.
- Repeated rows (lists, nav): use fixed-width slots for icons and trailing actions (flexShrink: 0); gap alone won't align columns across rows.
- When done creating or editing, you MUST call finish_working_on_nodes.
- Never show raw node IDs to the user.
- Export to the user's codebase: use get_jsx, get_computed_styles, get_fill_image, etc. for exact values — never read sizes or colors from screenshots.
</system-reminder>

1	import { CollectionPolicyHeader } from "@taxkit/analytics/schemas";
     2	import { TaxKitApiRoutesLayer } from "@taxkit/api-http/server";
     3	import { CalculatorRpcResponseTooLarge } from "@taxkit/api-rpc/errors";
     4	import {
     5	  CalculatorClientRateKey,
     6	  CalculatorHostMode,
     7	  CalculatorRequestRateKey,
     8	  calculatorEdgeRateKey,
     9	} from "@taxkit/api-rpc/rate-identity";
    10	import {
    11	  CalculatorRpcDeadline,
    12	  CalculatorRpcResponseLimit,
    13	} from "@taxkit/api-rpc/schemas";
    14	import { TaxKitRpcHttpLayer } from "@taxkit/api-rpc/server";
    15	import { PublicCalculatorService } from "@taxkit/calculators/service";
    16	import { DocsSourceError } from "@taxkit/content/errors";
    17	import { ContentDiscoveryLive } from "@taxkit/content/live";
    18	import { DocsDiscoverySettings } from "@taxkit/content/schemas";
    19	import { ContentCatalogue, ContentService } from "@taxkit/content/service";
    20	import { safeHttpEffect } from "alchemy/Http";
    21	import {
    22	  ByteSize,
    23	  Config,
    24	  Context,
    25	  Effect,
    26	  Layer,
    27	  Option,
    28	  Schema,
    29	  Scope,
    30	  Stream,
    31	} from "effect";
    32	import {
    33	  HttpClientRequest,
    34	  HttpClientResponse,
    35	  Headers,
    36	  HttpMiddleware,
    37	  HttpRouter,
    38	  HttpServerRequest,
    39	  HttpServerResponse,
    40	} from "effect/http";
    41	
    42	import {
    43	  ApiCalculatorDelivery,
    44	  withCalculatorAnalytics,
    45	} from "./analytics-request.boundary.js";
    46	import { ApiCalculatorEvents } from "./calculator-analytics.layer.js";
    47	import { McpRequestAbortSignal } from "./mcp-request.service.js";
    48	import { withBoundedMcpReply } from "./mcp-response.boundary.js";
    49	import { McpSessionHost } from "./mcp-session.layer.js";
    50	import { TaxKitMcpHttpLayer } from "./mcp.tools.layer.js";
    51	import { withApiRequestBodyLimit } from "./worker-request.boundary.js";
    52	import { ApiSafeTelemetryLive } from "./worker-telemetry.layer.js";
    53	import { ApiWorkerSettingsConfig } from "./worker.config.js";
    54	
    55	// Construct once in the native instance scope. Both transports receive this
    56	// same application service; native requests keep their own scope and fibre.
    57	export const ApiWorkerApplication = Effect.gen(function* () {
    58	  const analytics = yield* ApiCalculatorDelivery;
    59	  // Native planning binds deferred resource addresses. Read their runtime
    60	  // values once on first incoming use, without inventing planning URLs.
    61	  const settings = yield* Effect.cached(ApiWorkerSettingsConfig);
    62	  const localKey = yield* Effect.cached(
    63	    Config.schema(CalculatorHostMode, "CALCULATOR_HOST_MODE").pipe(
    64	      Config.withDefault("edge"),
    65	      Effect.flatMap((mode) =>
    66	        mode === "local-emulator"
    67	          ? settings.pipe(
    68	              Effect.flatMap((config) =>
    69	                config.apiOrigin.protocol === "http:" &&
    70	                (config.apiOrigin.hostname === "127.0.0.1" ||
    71	                  config.apiOrigin.hostname === "localhost")
    72	                  ? Schema.decodeEffect(CalculatorClientRateKey)(
    73	                      "127.0.0.1"
    74	                    ).pipe(Effect.map(Option.some))
    75	                  : Effect.succeed(Option.none())
    76	              )
    77	            )
    78	          : Effect.succeed(Option.none())
    79	      ),
    80	      Effect.catchTags({
    81	        ConfigError: () => Effect.succeedNone,
    82	        SchemaError: () => Effect.succeedNone,
    83	      })
    84	    )
    85	  );
    86	  const telemetry = yield* Layer.build(ApiSafeTelemetryLive);
    87	  const calculator = Layer.succeed(
    88	    PublicCalculatorService,
    89	    yield* PublicCalculatorService
    90	  );
    91	  const content = Layer.succeed(ContentService, yield* ContentService);
    92	  const discovery = ContentDiscoveryLive(
    93	    settings.pipe(
    94	      Effect.map((config) =>
    95	        DocsDiscoverySettings.make({
    96	          apiOrigin: config.apiOrigin,
    97	          websiteOrigin: config.websiteOrigin,
    98	        })
    99	      ),
   100	      Effect.mapError(
   101	        () =>
   102	          new DocsSourceError({
   103	            message: "Documentation discovery settings are unavailable.",
   104	            operation: "getDiscoveryDocument",
   105	          })
   106	      )
   107	    )
   108	  ).pipe(
   109	    Layer.provide(Layer.succeed(ContentCatalogue, yield* ContentCatalogue))
   110	  );
   111	  const routes = Layer.mergeAll(
   112	    TaxKitApiRoutesLayer,
   113	    TaxKitRpcHttpLayer.pipe(Layer.provide(calculator))
   114	  ).pipe(
   115	    Layer.provide(Layer.merge(content, discovery)),
   116	    HttpRouter.provideRequest(calculator)
   117	  );
   118	  const handler = yield* HttpRouter.toHttpEffect(routes).pipe(
   119	    Effect.provideContext(telemetry)
   120	  );
   121	  const instanceScope = yield* Scope.Scope;
   122	  const sessions = yield* McpSessionHost;
   123	  // Build the protocol host once on first use, after native addresses resolve.
   124	  // Retain its fibres in the instance Scope, and keep the first caller's
   125	  // request/key out of registration. Each call receives its own native Context.
   126	  const mcp = yield* Effect.cached(
   127	    settings.pipe(
   128	      Effect.flatMap((config) =>
   129	        HttpRouter.toHttpEffect(
   130	          TaxKitMcpHttpLayer(config.websiteOrigin).pipe(
   131	            Layer.provide(calculator),
   132	            Layer.provide(content)
   133	          )
   134	        )
   135	      ),
   136	      Scope.provide(instanceScope),
   137	      Effect.updateContext((context: Context.Context<never>) =>
   138	        Context.omit(
   139	          ApiCalculatorEvents,
   140	          CalculatorRequestRateKey,
   141	          McpRequestAbortSignal,
   142	          HttpServerRequest.HttpServerRequest
   143	        )(context)
   144	      ),
   145	      Effect.provideContext(telemetry),
   146	      Effect.catchTags({
   147	        ConfigError: () =>
   148	          Effect.succeed(
   149	            Effect.succeed(HttpServerResponse.empty({ status: 503 }))
   150	          ),
   151	        IllegalArgumentError: () =>
   152	          Effect.succeed(
   153	            Effect.succeed(HttpServerResponse.empty({ status: 503 }))
   154	          ),
   155	      })
   156	    )
   157	  );
   158	
   159	  const fetch = safeHttpEffect(
   160	    Effect.gen(function* () {
   161	      const config = yield* settings;
   162	      const request = yield* HttpServerRequest.HttpServerRequest;
   163	      const isMcp = new URL(request.url, config.apiOrigin).pathname === "/mcp";
   164	      const protocol = Headers.get(request.headers, "mcp-protocol-version");
   165	      const legacy =
   166	        Option.isSome(sessions) &&
   167	        Option.match(protocol, {
   168	          onNone: () => true,
   169	          onSome: (value) => value === "2025-11-25",
   170	        });
   171	      const selected = isMcp
   172	        ? (legacy && Option.isSome(sessions)
   173	            ? Effect.succeed(sessions.value.fetch)
   174	            : mcp
   175	          ).pipe(
   176	            Effect.flatMap(withBoundedMcpReply),
   177	            Effect.provideService(
   178	              McpRequestAbortSignal,
   179	              Schema.decodeUnknownOption(Schema.instanceOf(Request))(
   180	                request.source
   181	              ).pipe(Option.map((original) => original.signal))
   182	            )
   183	          )
   184	        : handler;
   185	      return yield* withCalculatorAnalytics(
   186	        withApiRequestBodyLimit(selected)
   187	      ).pipe(
   188	        Effect.provideService(ApiCalculatorDelivery, analytics),
   189	        HttpMiddleware.cors({
   190	          allowedHeaders: isMcp
   191	            ? [
   192	                CollectionPolicyHeader,
   193	                "content-type",
   194	                "mcp-method",
   195	                "mcp-name",
   196	                "mcp-protocol-version",
   197	                "mcp-session-id",
   198	              ]
   199	            : ["content-type", CollectionPolicyHeader],
   200	          allowedMethods: ["GET", "POST", "OPTIONS"],
   201	          // The native predicate checks the actual request origin.
   202	          allowedOrigins: (origin) => origin === config.websiteOrigin.origin,
   203	          credentials: false,
   204	        })
   205	      );
   206	    }).pipe(
   207	      Effect.catchTag("ConfigError", () =>
   208	        Effect.succeed(HttpServerResponse.empty({ status: 503 }))
   209	      )
   210	    )
   211	  ).pipe(Effect.provideContext(telemetry));
   212	
   213	  return {
   214	    // Native service-binding RPC only; this method has no HTTP route. The
   215	    // Website passes its checked original edge key separately from JSON.
   216	    calculatorRequest: (request: Request, encodedKey: string) =>
   217	      Effect.gen(function* () {
   218	        if (
   219	          Option.isNone(
   220	            Schema.decodeUnknownOption(Schema.instanceOf(Request))(request)
   221	          )
   222	        ) {
   223	          return new Response(null, { status: 503 });
   224	        }
   225	        if (
   226	          request.method !== "POST" ||
   227	          new URL(request.url).pathname !== "/rpc"
   228	        ) {
   229	          return new Response(null, { status: 404 });
   230	        }
   231	        const key = Schema.decodeUnknownOption(CalculatorClientRateKey)(
   232	          encodedKey
   233	        );
   234	        const response = yield* fetch.pipe(
   235	          Effect.provideService(CalculatorRequestRateKey, key),
   236	          Effect.provideService(
   237	            HttpServerRequest.HttpServerRequest,
   238	            HttpServerRequest.fromWeb(request)
   239	          )
   240	        );
   241	        // Buffer this closed JSON reply before the native method closes its
   242	        // event scope. Bound bytes and the complete read; it is not a stream.
   243	        const body = yield* HttpClientResponse.fromWeb(
   244	          HttpClientRequest.post(request.url),
   245	          HttpServerResponse.toWeb(response)
   246	        ).stream.pipe(
   247	          Stream.mapAccumEffect(
   248	            () => ByteSize.bytes(0),
   249	            (total, chunk) => {
   250	              const next = ByteSize.sum(
   251	                total,
   252	                ByteSize.bytes(chunk.byteLength)
   253	              );
   254	              return ByteSize.isGreaterThan(next, CalculatorRpcResponseLimit)
   255	                ? Effect.fail(new CalculatorRpcResponseTooLarge())
   256	                : Effect.succeed([next, [chunk]] as const);
   257	            }
   258	          ),
   259	          Stream.mkUint8Array,
   260	          Effect.timeoutOption(CalculatorRpcDeadline),
   261	          Effect.map(
   262	            Option.map(
   263	              (bytes) =>
   264	                new Response(new Uint8Array(bytes), {
   265	                  headers: response.headers,
   266	                  status: response.status,
   267	                })
   268	            )
   269	          ),
   270	          Effect.catchCause(() => Effect.succeed(Option.none<Response>()))
   271	        );
   272	        return Option.getOrElse(
   273	          body,
   274	          () => new Response(null, { status: 503 })
   275	        );
   276	      }).pipe(Effect.provideContext(telemetry)),
   277	    fetch: Effect.gen(function* () {
   278	      const request = yield* HttpServerRequest.HttpServerRequest;
   279	      const edgeKey = calculatorEdgeRateKey(request.headers);
   280	      const key = Option.isSome(edgeKey) ? edgeKey : yield* localKey;
   281	      return yield* fetch.pipe(
   282	        Effect.provideService(CalculatorRequestRateKey, key)
   283	      );
   284	    }),
   285	  };
   286	});

     1	import { Effect, Option } from "effect";
     2	
     3	import { McpRequestAbortSignal } from "./mcp-request.service.js";
     4	import { McpToolUnavailable } from "./mcp.schemas.js";
     5	
     6	// Native toolkit work must finish when its original HTTP request
     7	// disconnects. The native AbortSignal callback removes its listener on every exit;
     8	// raceFirst interrupts the losing work and waits for its scoped cleanup.
     9	export const withMcpRequestCancellation = Effect.fnUntraced(function* <A, E, R>(
    10	  operation: Effect.Effect<A, E, R>
    11	) {
    12	  const signal = yield* McpRequestAbortSignal;
    13	  if (Option.isNone(signal)) {
    14	    return yield* Effect.fail(
    15	      new McpToolUnavailable({
    16	        code: "service-unavailable",
    17	        retry: "try-again-manually",
    18	      })
    19	    );
    20	  }
    21	  if (signal.value.aborted) {
    22	    return yield* Effect.interrupt;
    23	  }
    24	  return yield* operation.pipe(
    25	    Effect.raceFirst(
    26	      // AbortSignal requires a synchronous host listener. Register first, then
    27	      // check again: cancellation can arrive before this race branch starts.
    28	      Effect.callback<never>((resume) => {
    29	        const abort = () => resume(Effect.interrupt);
    30	        signal.value.addEventListener("abort", abort, { once: true });
    31	        if (signal.value.aborted) {
    32	          abort();
    33	        }
    34	        return Effect.sync(() =>
    35	          signal.value.removeEventListener("abort", abort)
    36	        );
    37	      })
    38	    )
    39	  );
    40	});

    17	// status/size projection once; never expose its request, headers or body.
    18	const RejectedHttpStatus = Schema.TaggedStruct("StatusCodeError", {
    19	  response: Schema.Struct({ status: Schema.Literals([408, 413, 429]) }),
    20	});
    21	const OversizedHttpReply = Schema.TaggedStruct("DecodeError", {
    22	  cause: RpcResponseBodyTooLarge,
    23	});

    25	export const calculatorRpcTransportFailure = (
    26	  error: RpcClientError.RpcClientError
    27	) =>
    28	  Match.value(error.reason).pipe(
    29	    Match.tag("RpcClientDefect", () => new CalculatorRpcInvalidResponse()),
    30	    Match.tag("HttpError", (reason) =>
    31	      Schema.decodeUnknownOption(
    32	        Schema.Union([RejectedHttpStatus, OversizedHttpReply])
    33	      )(reason.cause).pipe(
    34	        Option.match({
    35	          onNone: () =>
    36	            Match.value(reason.kind).pipe(
    37	              Match.whenOr(
    38	                "DecodeError",
    39	                "EmptyBodyError",
    40	                () => new CalculatorRpcInvalidResponse()
    41	              ),
    42	              Match.orElse(() => new CalculatorRpcUnavailable())
    43	            ),
    44	          onSome: (rejection) =>
    45	            Match.value(rejection).pipe(
    46	              Match.tag(
    47	                "DecodeError",
    48	                () => new CalculatorRpcResponseTooLarge()
    49	              ),
    50	              Match.tag("StatusCodeError", ({ response }) =>
    51	                Match.value(response.status).pipe(
    52	                  Match.when(408, () => new CalculatorRpcRequestTimedOut()),
    53	                  Match.when(413, () => new CalculatorRpcRequestTooLarge()),
    54	                  Match.when(429, () => new CalculatorRateLimited()),

    59	            ),

    61	      )

content.text:
I mapped the API side end to end. Two items you asked about do not exist in this worktree: there is no `ALCHEMY_PHASE` check, and the API sets no `Cache-Control` headers. Paths below are relative to the worktree root.

## 1. apps/api (Cloudflare Worker)

**Entry and how it is built**
- **`apps/api/src/worker.ts`**
  - :87-95 declares `class TaxKitApiWorker extends Worker<…, { fetch: HttpEffect; calculatorRequest: … }>()("TaxKitApi")`.
  - :101-113 is the default export: `TaxKitApiWorker.make({ compatibility 2026-10-04 + nodejs_compat, env: { API_PUBLIC_ORIGIN: Worker.URL }, observability: ApiWorkerObservability (all off, :25-35), workersDev: true }, ApiWorkerNativeInit)`.
- **Service layer order (:37-51):** `PublicCalculatorServiceLive` → `PublicCalculatorServiceRateLimited` → `PublicCalculatorServiceBounded` (+ `CalculationEngineLive`) → `ApiCalculatorAnalyticsLive`, merged with `ApiContentLive`.
- **`ApiWorkerNativeInit` (:79-85)** adds `McpSessionHostLive`, `ApiAnalyticsLive` (PostHog via `FetchHttpClient`/`NodeCrypto`) and `ApiCalculatorAdmission` with `RateLimitBinding`. `TaxKitApiBinding` is at :97-99.
- **`apps/api/src/worker.application.ts`** (`ApiWorkerApplication`, :57):
  - Settings are read lazily with `Effect.cached(ApiWorkerSettingsConfig)` (:61), so origins resolve on first request, not during planning.
  - Routes (:111-117) are `TaxKitApiRoutesLayer` (built with `HttpApiBuilder.layer(TaxKitApi)` in `packages/api/http/src/server/live.layer.ts:17`) merged with `TaxKitRpcHttpLayer`. They are given content/discovery and use `HttpRouter.provideRequest(calculator)`. `HttpRouter.toHttpEffect(routes)` is at :118.
  - `fetch` (:159-211) is wrapped in `safeHttpEffect` from `alchemy/Http`. That function catches causes, returns 499 for interrupt-only and 500 otherwise. A `ConfigError` returns 503 (:207-209).
  - The public `fetch` (:277-284) gets its rate key from `calculatorEdgeRateKey(headers)`, falling back to `localKey`. `localKey` is 127.0.0.1 only when `CALCULATOR_HOST_MODE=local-emulator` and the API origin is http on localhost (:62-85).
- **Plan check:** nothing reads `ALCHEMY_PHASE`; grep finds it nowhere. Planning is detected instead in `apps/api/src/worker-admission.layer.ts:28-34`: `const runtime = yield* CurrentRuntimeContext; if (runtime === undefined) → admitCalculation fails CalculatorAdmissionUnavailable`.

**Private `calculatorRequest` capability** (`worker.application.ts:213-276`)
- It only accepts POST /rpc:
  - a non-`Request` input returns 503 (:218-224);
  - `request.method !== "POST" || pathname !== "/rpc"` returns 404 (:225-230).
- The rate key is decoded from the separate `encodedKey` argument (:231-233). The request then goes through the shared `fetch`.
- The reply is buffered: a byte-counting `Stream.mapAccumEffect` fails with `CalculatorRpcResponseTooLarge` above `CalculatorRpcResponseLimit` (2 MiB), followed by `Effect.timeoutOption(CalculatorRpcDeadline)` (10s) (:243-260).
- The `catchCause` site is :270: `Effect.catchCause(() => Effect.succeed(Option.none<Response>()))`, then `Option.getOrElse(… 503)` (:272-275). This also swallows interrupts.
- **Possible gap:** the 10s timeout wraps only the body-buffering stream. The `fetch` call at :234 runs before it.
- Caller: `apps/web/src/lib/live.server.layer.ts:50-69` (`toRpcAsync(...).calculatorRequest(incoming, formatIp(key))`). The binding is checked in `apps/web/src/lib/config.server.ts:11-20`.

**Bounded buffers**
| Limit | Location |
|---|---|
| Request body 64 KiB / 5s, POST only; 413 on size, 408 on deadline, plus a post-read clock check | `packages/api/http/src/request-boundary.ts:33-34, 39-123` (re-exported via `api-rpc/request-boundary` and `apps/api/src/worker-request.boundary.ts:1`); applied at `worker.application.ts:186` |
| RPC response 2 MiB / 10s | `packages/api/rpc/src/schemas.ts:60-61` |
| MCP response 2 MiB / 10s | `apps/api/src/mcp.schemas.ts:4-5` |
| Calculator work 5s budget; concurrency 8 (semaphore `withPermitsIfAvailable`, `CalculatorCapacityExceeded` when full) | `packages/calculators/src/work.layer.ts:9-10, 14-34, 42-56` |
| RPC ingress: ≤16 envelopes, ≤32 headers, ≤64 KiB | `packages/api/rpc/src/server-serialization.boundary.ts:19-60` |

**`catchCause` sites**
- `worker.application.ts:270`, described above.
- `apps/api/src/mcp-response.boundary.ts:42-48`: `timeoutOption(McpResponseDeadline)` wraps the handler and the buffering, then `catchCause((cause) => Cause.hasInterrupts(cause) ? Effect.interrupt : Effect.succeedNone)`, so failures become 503.
- Others: `apps/api/scripts/smoke-public-routes.runtime.ts:341` and `packages/api/http/src/client/server.layer.ts:27`.

**ErrorReporter**
- The API never calls `ErrorReporter.report`.
- `packages/api/rpc/src/host-telemetry.ts:14-25`: `ErrorReporter.make` logs the fixed message "Calculation host failure" with `Cause.empty`, as JSON event `api.runtime.event`. It is wired through `apps/api/src/worker-telemetry.layer.ts:3` (`CalculatorHostTelemetryLive("api")`) and provided at `worker.application.ts:86, 119, 145, 211, 276`.
- Explicit `report` calls exist only in `apps/web/src/server.ts:265-268` and `apps/web/src/lib/loaders.server.ts:43-147`.

**CORS** (`worker.application.ts:189-204`)
- Uses `HttpMiddleware.cors`.
- `allowedOrigins: (origin) => origin === config.websiteOrigin.origin`, `allowedMethods: ["GET","POST","OPTIONS"]`, `credentials: false`.
- Headers: `["content-type", CollectionPolicyHeader]`. For /mcp it adds `mcp-method`, `mcp-name`, `mcp-protocol-version` and `mcp-session-id`.
- `traceparent` is not allowed. Tracing is disabled instead, which keeps it off requests:
  - server: `RpcServer.layerHttp({ disableTracing: true, protocol: "http", path: "/rpc" })` (`packages/api/rpc/src/server.ts:10-15`);
  - clients: `RpcClient.make(..., { disableTracing: true })` plus `TracerDisabledWhen → true` and `RequestInit { credentials: "omit", redirect: "error" }` (`packages/api/rpc/src/live.layer.ts:66-72`; `content.live.layer.ts:60-66`).

**MCP**
- **Modern:** `TaxKitMcpHttpLayer(websiteOrigin, protocol = McpProtocol.v2026_07_28)` uses `McpServer.layerHttp({ allowedOrigins: [websiteOrigin.origin], path: "/mcp", name: "TaxKit", version: "1" })` (`apps/api/src/mcp.tools.layer.ts:209-224`). It has 6 tools (:24-90), and each handler is wrapped in `withMcpRequestCancellation` (`mcp-cancellation.boundary.ts`, an AbortSignal race).
  - It is built once with `Effect.cached` in the instance `Scope`, with request-scoped services omitted (`worker.application.ts:126-157`).
- **Legacy:** chosen when the session host exists and `mcp-protocol-version` is absent or `2025-11-25` (`worker.application.ts:164-176`). It routes to the Durable Object `TaxKitMcpSessions` via `getByName("legacy-mcp-v2025-11-25")`. The trusted key travels in header `x-taxkit-mcp-calculator-key`; any incoming copy is stripped first (`apps/api/src/mcp-session.layer.ts:62, 277-291`).
- **Early protection in the DO fetch:** path ≠ /mcp → 404; bad Origin → 403 *before* state allocation (:158-165); malformed session id → 404; non-POST → 405. An expired or unknown id cannot create a host (:200-203). Each host allows 32 initialisations, then 429 with `retry-after` (:212-236). Requests are capped at 32 via a semaphore, then 503 (:131, 259-264). Sessions last 10 minutes and expire by alarm (:86-116, 132-148; constants in `mcp.schemas.ts:6-8`).

**Rate limit**
- `apps/api/src/worker-admission.layer.ts:20-27`: `RateLimit("CALCULATOR_RATE_LIMIT", { namespaceId: CALCULATOR_RATE_NAMESPACE, simple: { limit: 60, period: 60 } })`, keyed by `NetAddress.formatIp(key)`.
- Applied by `PublicCalculatorServiceRateLimited` (`packages/calculators/src/admission.layer.ts:12-33`); a missing key gives `CalculatorAdmissionUnavailable`.
- HTTP 429 carries `retry-after: "60"` (`packages/api/http/src/groups/calculators.ts:76-89`).

**Cache-Control:** none is set anywhere in `apps/api/src` or `packages/{api,content,calculators}/src`. The only headers set are the `retry-after` ones above. Cache headers live in the Website:
- `apps/web/src/server.ts:103` sets `"public, max-age=300"` on discovery documents;
- `"no-store"` appears at `server.ts:68,117`, `markdown.response.server.ts:52,94,119,127` (which also sets `public, max-age=300` at :103), and `relay.adapter.layer.ts:24`.

**Discovery documents**
- The formatter is `ContentDiscoveryLive(settings)` in `packages/content/src/live.layer.ts:81-169`. It builds `/sitemap.xml`, `/robots.txt`, `/llms.txt` (links to `${apiOrigin}/api/v1/docs/markdown?path=…`) and `/llms-full.txt` (canonical links use `websiteOrigin`).
- The API exposes them only as RPC `GetDocsDiscovery` (`packages/api/rpc/src/content.group.ts:44-49`; handler `content.handlers.ts:18-29`). There is no HTTP route on the API; the Website serves the paths (`apps/web/src/server.ts:88-121`).

**Origins and Outputs**
- `apps/api/src/worker.config.ts:5-24` reads `API_PUBLIC_ORIGIN` and `WEBSITE_PUBLIC_ORIGIN`, validated by `ApiWorkerSettings` (`apps/api/src/schemas.ts:37-40`).
- In `packages/infrastructure/src/apps-stack.ts`, the API gets `WEBSITE_PUBLIC_ORIGIN: website.url.pipe(Output.map(...))` (:92-98). The Website gets `API_PUBLIC_ORIGIN: api.url` via `Output.map`, plus `TAXKIT_API: api` (:34-58).

## 2. Bun host
- It lives in `apps/api/src/index.ts`, which runs `BunRuntime.runMain` on `ApiAppLayer`. `server.ts:20-23` serves `HttpRouter.serve(TaxKitServerLayer)` over `BunHttpServer` (`API_HOST`/`API_PORT`/`PORT`, default 127.0.0.1:4000, `config.ts:19-70`). Scripts are `dev` and `start` (`apps/api/package.json`).
- It serves only the HTTP API: health, calculators, docs, Scalar at `/api/docs` and `/api/docs/openapi.json`. There is no RPC, MCP, rate limiting or analytics.
- CORS is `HttpRouter.cors()` with defaults, which means `access-control-allow-origin: *`.
- Composition is in `packages/api/http/src/server/live.layer.ts:41-50`: `HttpRouter.provideRequest(PublicCalculatorServiceBounded ← Live ← CalculationEngineLive)` plus the body-limit middleware.
- **No per-request capacity pool.** `provideRequest` runs `Layer.build` once when the middleware is built (effect `HttpRouter.ts:1304-1321`), so there is one semaphore per serve or per built layer. `TaxKitApiInProcessClientLive` likewise builds it once per layer build.

## 3. packages/api/http
- **`TaxKitApi`** (`src/api.ts:7-15`) contains these groups and endpoints:
  - **health** (prefix `/api`, `groups/health.ts:9-16`): GET `/api/health`.
  - **calculatorApi** (prefix `/api/v1`, `groups/calculators.ts:121-232`):
    - GET `/jurisdictions`, `/tax-years`, `/calculators`
    - GET `/calculators/:calculatorId`, `/calculators/:calculatorId/schema`, `/calculators/:calculatorId/graph`
    - POST `/calculators/:calculatorId/calculate`
    - GET `/facts`, `/rules`
  - **content** (prefix `/api/v1/docs`, `groups/content.ts:31-73`): GET `/navigation`, `/page`, `/search`, `/markdown` (text/markdown).
  - Extra routes: GET `/api/docs` (Scalar) and GET `/api/docs/openapi.json` (`server/live.layer.ts:23-31`).
- **Helpers:**
  - `createTaxKitApiClient` and the deprecated `makeTaxKitApiClient`: `src/client/index.ts:12-20`.
  - `TaxKitHttpApiService`, its alias `getTaxKitHttpApiClient`, and `withTaxKitHttpApiClient`: `src/client/service.ts:5-18`.
  - `createTaxKitApiClientLayer` and the deprecated `makeTaxKitApiClientLayer`: `src/client/live.layer.ts:12-19`.
  - `TaxKitApiInProcessClientLive`: `src/client/server.layer.ts:17-42`.
- **Users:**

## 4. packages/api/rpc
- **Groups** (`src/group.ts:89-101`): `TaxKitRpcGroup` has Calculate, GetCalculator, GetCalculatorGraph, GetCalculatorSchema, ListCalculators, ListFacts, ListJurisdictions, ListRules and ListTaxYears. It merges with `DocsRpcGroup` (GetDocsNavigation, GetDocsPage, SearchDocsPages, GetDocsMarkdown, GetDocsDiscovery) to form `TaxKitPublicRpcGroup`. `CalculatorRpcVersion = "4"` (`schemas.ts:29`).
- **`src/rate-identity.boundary.ts:14-21`:** if a `cf-worker` header is present the result is `Option.none()`, because same-zone subrequests can alter IPs. Otherwise it decodes `cf-connecting-ip` as `CalculatorClientRateKey`. `CalculatorHostMode = "edge" | "local-emulator"` (:8).
- **Bounded client adapter** (`src/response-budget.boundary.ts:13-53`, `boundedRpcHttpClient`):
  - applies `HttpClient.withScope`, then `HttpClient.filterStatusOk`;
  - counts bytes up to 2 MiB and fails with `DecodeError(cause: RpcResponseBodyTooLarge)`;
  - rebuilds the reply as `new Response(new Uint8Array(bytes), { headers })`, with no status, so it defaults to 200;
  - is wired in `live.layer.ts:211-224` (URL set to `/rpc` on the origin) and `content.live.layer.ts:158`.
- **Failure mapping** (`client-response.boundary.ts:18-64`): status 408 → `RequestTimedOut`, 413 → `RequestTooLarge`, 429 → `CalculatorRateLimited`, oversize → `ResponseTooLarge`, anything else → Unavailable or InvalidResponse.

## 7. packages/content
- **`src/schemas.ts`:**
  - `PublicHttpOrigin` (:4-12) accepts origin-only URLs that are https, or http on localhost/127.0.0.1.
  - `DocsWebsiteOrigin` is that schema branded (:13-15).
  - `DocsDiscoverySettings { apiOrigin: PublicHttpOrigin, websiteOrigin: DocsWebsiteOrigin }` (:17-20).
  - `DocsDiscoveryPath` covers the 4 paths (:22-27); bodies are capped at 300,000 characters (:31-33); the content type must match the path (:34-45).
  - There is no `publicOrigin` field anywhere; grep finds only `API_PUBLIC_ORIGIN` and `WEBSITE_PUBLIC_ORIGIN` environment keys.
- **`src/live.layer.ts:81-88`:** `ContentDiscoveryLive(settings: Effect<DocsDiscoverySettings, DocsSourceError>)` caches the settings Effect and resolves it on first use. The API supplies it at `worker.application.ts:92-110`.
- `CalculatorRpcOrigin` (`packages/api/rpc/src/schemas.ts:55-57`) is `PublicHttpOrigin` with an RPC brand.
